newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy back in Israel to help in Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy back in Israel to help in Hebron deal.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross arrived back in Israel on Monday to mediate any last-minute snags in the Hebron deal, U.S. officials said.
Ross and other members of his negotiating team left Washington on Sunday for the region.
Israeli and Palestinian officials said on Monday that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ready to hand over the occupied West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.

Palestinian negotiator Mahmoud Abbas said the long-elusive deal to transfer 80 percent of Hebron would probably be signed at a summit on Tuesday between Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and Netanyahu, the Likud party leader elected in May.
Ross last week pushed and pulled the sides together on orders from U.S. President Bill Clinton, then returned to Washington for a few days.

Under pressure from the United States, Israel's closest ally, Netanyahu stayed in the negotiations while emphasising that 20 percent of the town, including Hebron's Jews and the tomb of the biblical patriarch Abraham, would remain under Israeli control.

Hebron, long a flashpoint of violence between Arabs and Jews, is the last of seven West Bank towns scheduled for Palestinian self-rule under an agreement signed in 1995. It was due to have been given self-rule nine months ago, but security concerns held up the handover.
